title_en: Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. — dispute over patent assignment contract
ruling_gist_en: Where a patent right is declared invalid, previously concluded patent licensing or assignment contracts shall not be rendered invalid due to such invalidation. If the performance of such contracts becomes impossible due to the invalidation of the patent right, the parties may claim modification or rescission of the contract on this basis. Whether all unperformed parts of the contract after the patent right is declared invalid should no longer be performed shall be determined based on whether the interests involved in the unperformed part are directly obtained from the exercise of the patent right. Patent licensing fees, assignment fees, and damages for infringement are all consideration for the value of the patent right. After the patent right is declared invalid, the right holder has no right to demand continued performance. If the unperformed part concerns liquidated damages payable due to a party's breach of contract, since liquidated damages generally do not directly correspond to the value of the patent right but correspond to the breaching conduct of the party, the declaration of invalidity of the patent right does not have retroactive effect in this regard, and the patentee is entitled to demand the breaching party to continue performing the unpaid liquidated damages.

full_text_en:
Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. — dispute over patent assignment contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a patent right is declared invalid, a patent licensing or assignment contract previously concluded is not rendered invalid for that reason. If such a contract cannot be performed due to the invalidation of the patent, the parties may claim modification or rescission of the contract on that basis. Whether the unperformed portion of the contract after the patent has been declared invalid is no longer to be performed in its entirety shall be determined by whether the interests involved in the unperformed portion are directly derived from the exercise of the patent right. Patent royalties, assignment fees, damages for infringement, etc., are all consideration for the value of the patent right. Once the patent right is declared invalid, the right holder has no right to demand continued performance. If the unperformed portion consists of liquidated damages payable due to a party's breach of contract, since liquidated damages are generally not directly corresponding to the value of the patent right but rather to the party's breach, the invalidation of the patent right has no retroactive effect in this regard, and the patentee is entitled to demand that the breaching party continue to perform with respect to the unpaid liquidated damages.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court IP Civil Final No. 394

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 202A, Building 1, No. 8 Hangfeng Road, Science City, Fengtai District, Beijing (Park Area).

Legal Representative: Li Hong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Shen Bin, lawyer of Beijing Lingchuang Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 320, Building 1, No. 8 Hangfeng Road, Science City, Fengtai District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Li Yining, General Manager of the Company.

The appellant, Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Langkun Company), appealed to this Court from the civil judgment (2018) Jing 73 Min Chu No. 1132 rendered by the Beijing Intellectual Property Court on May 22, 2019, in a dispute over a patent assignment contract with the respondent, Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huilang Company). After the case was docketed on August 26, 2019, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on October 23, 2019. Shen Bin, agent ad litem of the appellant Langkun Company, and Li Yining, agent ad litem of the respondent Huilang Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Langkun Company's appeal requests: to revoke the original judgment in accordance with the law and to amend the judgment to support the claims of Langkun Company at the first instance. Facts and reasons: 1. According to the terms of the "Patent Assignment Agreement" signed by both parties, Huilang Company could not assign the patent-in-suit to any third party, and if it did so, it should pay liquidated damages of RMB 1 million to Langkun Company. In 2017, Liu Junxia, the chairperson of Huilang Company, without the consent and knowledge of other shareholders, privately controlled the company seal of Huilang Company and assigned the patent-in-suit to a third party, Cai Limin. The unauthorized assignment by Huilang Company violated the terms of the agreement and should incur liability for liquidated damages of RMB 1 million. 2. Although the patent-in-suit was declared invalid, the reason for its invalidation was that Cai Limin handled the invalidation procedure improperly. The patent-in-suit could have been maintained valid by amending the claims during the invalidation proceedings. 3. According to Article 47 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law), the invalidation of the patent-in-suit does not affect the validity of "a patent exploitation licensing contract or a patent assignment contract that has already been performed." Huilang Company's breach of contract occurred before the patent-in-suit was declared invalid, and it was due to Huilang Company's breach that the assignee Cai Limin acted passively and negatively in the invalidation proceedings, leading to the invalidation of the patent-in-suit. Therefore, Huilang Company should bear liability for liquidated damages in accordance with the agreement. 4. Huilang Company's unauthorized assignment of the patent-in-suit resulted in unjust enrichment of RMB 1 million, and the patent-in-suit had extremely high commercial value. Langkun Company's claim for RMB 1 million in liquidated damages from Huilang Company is not improper.

Huilang Company argues: Liu Junxia, a shareholder of Huilang Company, controlled the company seal of Huilang Company and the patent-in-suit. Liu Junxia, without the knowledge of other shareholders, privately assigned the patent-in-suit to a third party, Cai Limin. Huilang Company had no knowledge of this. The original court found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and Huilang Company accepts the original court's judgment.

Langkun Company filed a lawsuit with the original court, which accepted the case on October 24, 2018. Langkun Company's claims were: 1. to rescind the "Patent Assignment Agreement" entered into between Langkun Company and Huilang Company; 2. that Huilang Company return all technical materials and drawings that had been delivered; 3. that Huilang Company pay Langkun Company liquidated damages of RMB 1 million; and 4. that the litigation costs of this case be borne by Huilang Company. During the original trial, Langkun Company clearly stated that it would no longer pursue claims 1 and 2.

Facts Found by the Original Court:

I. Facts concerning the patent-in-suit and the agreement-in-suit

The patent-in-suit is an invention patent titled "Biological Protection Filtration Medium and Its Application," patent number ZL201110145600.3, with a filing date of June 1, 2011, and a grant and announcement date of June 12, 2013. The patentee was originally Li Hong, and on September 3, 2014, it was changed to Langkun Company.

On May 5, 2015, Langkun Company (as Party A) and Huilang Company (as Party B) entered into the agreement-in-suit, which included the following content: Langkun Company (Party A) intends to transfer the patent-in-suit to Huilang Company (Party B). After discussions, the parties reached the following agreement: 1. Party A agrees to transfer the patent gratuitously to Party B for patent transformation. 2. Party B shall not transfer the patent to any third party. 3. Party A shall not disclose or transfer in any form the core technical secrets of the patent to any third party. 4. If Party B's business develops into difficulties in the future and is on the verge of bankruptcy, the patent shall be transferred back to Party A without compensation. 5. If after the transfer of the patent, due to Party A's fault, the patent cannot be used normally, all consequences arising therefrom shall be borne by Party A. 6. Any party that violates the above agreement must pay liquidated damages of RMB one million yuan to the other party. 7. The parties shall complete the patent transfer procedures at the State Intellectual Property Office within 10 days after signing this agreement. 8. This agreement is made in triplicate, with each party holding one copy and one copy filed with the State Intellectual Property Office for record.

On June 24, 2015, the patentee of the patent-in-suit was changed to Huilang Company upon approval.

On December 21, 2016, the patentee of the patent-in-suit was changed to Cai Limin, a third party.

On June 9, 2017, a third party, Hangke Zhongtou Biotechnology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hangke Company), filed a request for invalidation of the patent-in-suit with the former Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board). On September 28, 2018, the Patent Reexamination Board issued the Invalidation Request Examination Decision No. 37403 (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 37403) regarding the above invalidation request, declaring the patent-in-suit completely invalid. The specific reason was that claims 1-8 of the patent-in-suit did not comply with the provisions of Article 22, paragraph 2 or paragraph 3 of the Patent Law. Huilang Company stated at trial that, according to its understanding, Cai Limin did not file an administrative lawsuit against that decision. After verification by the original court, no party filed an administrative lawsuit against Decision No. 37403, and the decision has become effective.

The above facts are supported by the following evidence submitted by Langkun Company (the authenticity, legality, and relevance of which are not disputed by Huilang Company): the "Invention Patent Certificate" for the patent-in-suit, the published text of the patent-in-suit, the "Patent Assignment Agreement," the inquiry form for the change in patent status, Decision No. 37403, and the trial transcripts.

II. Relevant evidence submitted by Langkun Company to prove that Huilang Company constituted a breach of contract

Langkun Company submitted the following evidence to prove that Huilang Company breached the contract:

1. The "Resolution of the Interim Shareholders' Meeting of Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd." (2018 Resolution No. 1) dated October 25, 2018, which recorded the adoption of the following resolution: Huilang Company shall be liquidated and dissolved. The expenses related to liquidation shall be borne by each shareholder according to their shareholding ratio. The "Resolution of the Interim Shareholders' Meeting of Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd." (2018 Resolution No. 2) dated October 25, 2018, which recorded the adoption of the following resolution: The relevant seals, articles, etc., of Huilang Company shall be returned by Chairperson Liu Junxia to the legal representative Li Yining for custody in accordance with the list provided by Yang Weijian. Both shareholders' resolutions bear the signatures of shareholders including Li Hong, Li Yining, and Liu Junxia. This evidence was used to prove that Huilang Company was in financial difficulty and should have transferred the patent-in-suit back to Langkun Company in accordance with the agreement.

2. The "Resolution of the Interim Shareholders' Meeting of Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd." (2018 Resolution No. 3) dated October 25, 2018, which recorded the adoption of the following resolution: The patent should return to this company, and the "Patent Assignment Agreement" signed by this company and Langkun Company on May 5, 2015, should continue to be observed. This shareholders' resolution bears the signatures of shareholders including Li Hong, Li Yining, and Liu Junxia. This evidence was used to prove that the shareholders' resolution of Huilang Company recognized the content agreed upon in the agreement.

3. The civil judgment No. (2016) Jing 0106 Min Chu No. 19956 (Judgment No. 19956) rendered by the Fengtai District People's Court of Beijing on January 11, 2017, which ordered Huilang Company to repay a loan of RMB 1 million to Cai Limin.

At the original trial, Langkun Company stated that because Huilang Company owed Cai Limin RMB 1 million, the patent-in-suit was transferred to Cai Limin. After the patent-in-suit was transferred to Cai Limin, a third party filed an invalidation request against the patent-in-suit. According to Decision No. 37403 issued by the Patent Reexamination Board, Cai Limin did not conduct a proper defense in the patent invalidation proceedings, resulting in the invalidation of the patent-in-suit.

The above facts are supported by the following evidence submitted by Langkun Company (the authenticity, legality, and relevance of which are not disputed by Huilang Company): shareholders' resolutions of Huilang Company, Judgment No. 19956, and trial transcripts.

Huilang Company submitted the civil judgment No. (2016) Jing 0108 Min Chu No. 36578 (Judgment No. 36578) rendered by the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing on August 31, 2018, to prove that Huilang Company was unable to affix its company seal on certain materials because the company seal was in the hands of Liu Junxia, and that Huilang Company had filed a lawsuit regarding this matter. Langkun Company did not object to the authenticity, legality, or relevance of this evidence.

The above facts are supported by the evidence submitted by Huilang Company (Judgment No. 36578) and the trial transcripts.

The original court held that, given that the patent-in-suit had been declared invalid, the already performed portions of the agreement should not be retroactively affected, and the unperformed portions could be left unperformed. Furthermore, although the penalty clause in the agreement stipulated liquidated damages of RMB 1 million, the invalidation of the patent-in-suit was due to inherent problems with the patent itself, not caused by Huilang Company's breach of contract. Therefore, Langkun Company's claim for an order that Huilang Company pay liquidated damages for transferring the patent-in-suit to a third party, after the patent-in-suit had been declared invalid, lacked factual and legal basis.

The original court ruled: Reject all claims of Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd.

The court fee for the first instance was RMB 13,800, to be borne by Langkun Company.

During the second instance of this Court, Langkun Company, to support its contentions, additionally submitted two pieces of evidence: Langkun Company's business registration information (including an asset appraisal report for the patent technology) and promotional materials for the patent technology by Hangke Company, to demonstrate that the patent technology possessed high market value. Huilang Company acknowledged and had no objection to these two pieces of evidence. This Court holds that Huilang Company had no objection to the evidence submitted by Langkun Company, and the asset appraisal report for the patent technology is relevant to this case to a certain extent, so this Court admits it. The promotional materials for the patent technology by Hangke Company are irrelevant to this case, and this Court does not admit them.

Additionally, upon Langkun Company's application, this Court obtained from the State Intellectual Property Office evidence such as the assignment contract when the patent-in-suit was transferred from Huilang Company to Cai Limin. Langkun Company and Huilang Company acknowledged the evidence obtained by this Court.

This Court finds, upon trial, that the facts found by the original court are essentially correct, and this Court confirms them.

This Court additionally finds:

On November 23, 2016, Huilang Company and Cai Limin entered into a "Patent Assignment Contract," which, according to Articles 5 and 8 thereof, provided that Huilang Company would gratuitously transfer the invention patent rights specified in the contract to Cai Limin. The contract bears the seal of Huilang Company at its execution section.

The civil judgment No. (2016) Jing 0108 Min Chu No. 36578 of the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing records the following: Liu Junxia, as the registered chairperson and former legal representative of Huilang Company, held the certificates, seals, and related items of Huilang Company, which did not violate legal provisions or the company's articles of association. Therefore, the court dismissed Huilang Company's claim requiring Liu Junxia to return the company seal, etc. As of the date of the second instance trial, this judgment had not yet taken effect.

According to the "Asset Appraisal Report on Biological Protection Medium Technology (Jing Rong Ping Bao Zi [2013] No. 012)" in the business registration materials of Langkun Company, with the market value as of January 18, 2013, as the appraisal base date, the appraised asset value of the intellectual property—non-patent technology "Biological Protection Medium Technology" owned by the entrusting party was RMB 8 million.

During the second instance trial, after being prompted by this Court, Huilang Company stated that if the court determined that it should bear liability for liquidated damages, the amount of liquidated damages stipulated in the contract was too high, and it requested the court to adjust it. Langkun Company stated that, aside from the value of the patent-in-suit, it had no other evidence to prove its actual losses.

During the second instance trial, Langkun Company stated that claim 1 of the patent-in-suit could be amended in the invalidation proceedings as follows: "1. A biological protection filtration medium, comprising an adsorption layer, characterized in that the adsorption layer is a fiber layer having virus-, bacteria-, or allergen-specific binding receptors or ligands immobilized on its surface, and the specific binding receptors or ligands immobilized on the surface of the adsorption layer include sialic acid and its derivatives, L-polylysine, ε-polylysine, or Toll-like receptors and polymyxin B; wherein the derivative of sialic acid is mucin." Langkun Company stated that such an amendment could have sustained the validity of the patent-in-suit.

During the original trial, Langkun Company confirmed that the basis for claiming liquidated damages of RMB 1 million from Huilang Company in this case was Articles 2, 4, and 6 of the Assignment Agreement, and it no longer pursued the claim for rescission of the contract.

The above facts are supported by the "Patent Assignment Contract" obtained by this Court, the civil judgment No. (2016) Jing 0108 Min Chu No. 36578 of the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, the appraisal report for the patent-in-suit, and the statements of the parties, all of which are on file, and this Court confirms them.

This Court holds that the issue in dispute in this case is whether Huilang Company should pay liquidated damages to Langkun Company. Specifically, this involves the following sub-issues: 1. Whether Huilang Company committed a breach of contract by unauthorizedly assigning the patent-in-suit; 2. If Huilang Company constituted a breach, whether Langkun Company could claim liquidated damages from Huilang Company under the "Patent Assignment Agreement" after the patent-in-suit was declared invalid; and 3. If Huilang Company should bear liquidated damages, the specific amount of liquidated damages that it should bear.

I. Whether Huilang Company committed a breach of contract by unauthorizedly assigning the patent-in-suit

According to Article 2 of the "Patent Assignment Agreement," Huilang Company was not to transfer the patent to any third party. In this case, the patentee of the patent-in-suit was changed from Huilang Company to the third party Cai Limin on December 21, 2016. The assignment contract bore the seal of Huilang Company, and it should be determined that Huilang Company carried out the act of assigning the patent-in-suit, thereby violating the provisions of the "Patent Assignment Agreement."

As to Huilang Company's argument that the assignment of the patent-in-suit was a personal act by its chairperson Liu Junxia and was unrelated to Huilang Company, this Court holds: Since Liu Junxia was the chairperson of the company and held the company seal, and in the absence of sufficient contrary evidence proving that there were special provisions regarding Liu Junxia's authority within Huilang Company, the legal consequences of affixing the company seal on the "Patent Assignment Contract" entered into with the third party Cai Limin shall be borne by Huilang Company. This Court does not accept Huilang Company's relevant argument.

II. Whether Langkun Company could claim liquidated damages from Huilang Company under the "Patent Assignment Agreement"

Article 47, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Patent Law provide: "Any patent right which has been declared invalid shall be deemed to have been non-existent from the beginning. The decision declaring a patent right invalid shall have no retroactive effect on any judgment or mediation decision on patent infringement which has been pronounced and enforced by a people's court prior to the declaration of invalidation, on any decision concerning the handling of a patent infringement dispute which has been performed or compulsorily executed, or on any patent exploitation licensing contract or patent assignment contract which has been performed prior to the declaration of invalidation. However, any loss caused to another person by the patentee's bad faith shall be compensated." The above provisions clarify the relevant legal consequences after a patent right is declared invalid, but two issues still need to be explored: first, the validity of a patent exploitation licensing contract or assignment contract entered into before the patent right is declared invalid; and second, whether the invalidation of the patent right has a retroactive effect on unperformed liabilities for breach of contract.

First, regarding the validity of a patent exploitation licensing contract or assignment contract entered into before the patent right is declared invalid. Article 143 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A civil juristic act shall be valid if it meets the following conditions: (1) the actor has the corresponding capacity for civil conduct; (2) the intention expressed is genuine; and (3) it does not violate the mandatory provisions of the law or administrative regulations, and does not contravene public order and good customs." Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract shall be null and void under any of the following circumstances: (1) one party induced the conclusion of the contract through fraud or duress, thereby harming the interests of the state; (2) there was malicious collusion harming the interests of the state, the collective, or a third party; (3) an illegal purpose was concealed under the guise of a lawful form; (4) the public interest was harmed; or (5) mandatory provisions of the law or administrative regulations were violated." The declaration of invalidity of a patent right means that the subject matter of the patent licensing or assignment contract no longer exists, making it objectively impossible to perform the contract. However, according to the above provisions, the declaration of invalidity of a patent right is not a cause for a contract to be null and void. If the relevant contract represents the true intention of the parties, does not violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, does not contravene public order and good customs, and there is no other cause for its invalidity, then, considering the value of upholding party autonomy and promoting transactions, it cannot be held that a patent licensing or assignment contract entered into before the invalidation is also invalid simply because the patent right is later declared invalid. The consequence for the performance of the contract arising from the invalidation of the patent right is the impossibility of performing the obligations related to the patent right. Since the contract objectively cannot be performed further, the parties may claim rescission of the contract, and the rights and obligations under the contract shall be terminated.

Second, regarding whether the invalidation of a patent has retroactive effect on liability for breach of contract that remains unperformed. After a patent is invalidated, in principle, the invalidation has retroactive effect on the part that has already been performed, but given the public trust in patent grants and to maintain existing social order, in principle, the invalidation has no retroactive effect on patent infringement judgments, mediation agreements, administrative decisions, and license or assignment contracts that have been made and executed. As to whether the part that remains unperformed at the time of the patent's invalidation shall no longer be performed in all cases, it is necessary to consider whether the interests involved in the unperformed part are interests directly obtained from exercising the patent right, i.e., the consideration for the value of the patent, such as license fees, assignment fees, damages for infringement, etc. For such interests, since the patent has been invalidated, the right holder naturally has no right to demand continued performance. If the interests involved in the unperformed part are not the consideration for the value of the patent, but rather damages caused to the patent holder by the other party's breach of contract or unauthorized acts, which generally are not directly related to the value of the patent itself, then the patent holder is entitled to demand the other party to continue performance.

Therefore, the invalidation of a patent does not affect the validity of a patent license contract or assignment contract entered into before the invalidation. Whether the unperformed part before the invalidation shall not be performed in all cases requires examination and determination of whether the unperformed part constitutes benefits directly obtained from exercising the patent right. License fees, assignment fees, damages for infringement, etc., are considerations based on the patent, and after the patent is invalidated, the unperformed part shall not be performed. If the liquidated damages stipulated in the contract are not directly corresponding to the value of the patent but rather compensate for other losses caused to the non-breaching party by the breach, beyond the value of the patent, the non-breaching party is entitled to demand the breaching party to continue performance.

In this case: On one hand, Article 2 of the Patent Assignment Agreement stipulates: "Party B shall not assign the patent to any third party." Article 6 stipulates: "Any party that breaches the above agreement must pay liquidated damages of RMB 1,000,000 to the other party." The above stipulations are clear provisions by both parties regarding their respective rights and obligations when signing the patent assignment contract. They not only serve as a pre-agreed determination of damages but also function as a guarantee for the proper conclusion and performance of the contract. The above arrangement of rights and obligations voluntarily negotiated by both parties should be respected and protected, and should not be rendered invalid merely because the patent in question was subsequently invalidated. On the other hand, the provision in the contract concerning liability for liquidated damages for unauthorized assignment of the patent protects other interests independent of the value of the patent that are worthy of protection. Such interests include not only the patent holder's reliance interest and expectation interest in the normal performance of the contract, but also the sanction against Huilang Company's unauthorized breach. This liquidated damages provision is not directly corresponding to the value of the patent itself, but rather serves to constrain the parties' conduct and ensure that they strictly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the contract. In fact, when Huilang Company unilaterally assigned the patent to a third party, the patent was valid. Huilang Company knew it could not assign the patent to a third party but still breached the contract, and it should bear the corresponding adverse consequences. Otherwise, if Huilang Company were relieved of its liability for breach merely because the patent was subsequently invalidated, Langkun Company's interest in the normal performance of the contract would not be protected, and this would also improperly condone the breaching party.

Therefore, after the patent in question was invalidated, the Patent Assignment Agreement signed between Huilang Company and Langkun Company remains valid, and Huilang Company shall still bear corresponding liability for its breach of contract in unilaterally assigning the patent to a third party before the patent's invalidation.

III. Amount of Liquidated Damages to Be Borne by Huilang Company

Article 114, Paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "If the agreed liquidated damages are lower than the losses caused, the parties may request the people's court or an arbitration institution to increase them; if the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused, the parties may request the people's court or an arbitration institution to reduce them appropriately." Article 174 provides: "For other contracts for value, if other laws provide otherwise, those provisions shall apply; if not, the relevant provisions on sales contracts shall apply by reference." Article 27 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Sales Contracts (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation on Sales Contract Disputes) provides: "If one party to a sales contract claims payment of liquidated damages on the ground that the other party has breached the contract, and the other party raises a defense of exemption, such as the contract not being established, not taking effect, being invalid, or not constituting a breach, without claiming adjustment of the excessively high liquidated damages, the people's court shall provide clarification as to whether the party needs to claim adjustment of the liquidated damages if the court does not support the defense of exemption. If the court of first instance considers that the defense of exemption is established and does not provide clarification, and the court of second instance considers that payment of liquidated damages should be ordered, it may directly provide clarification and amend the judgment." Article 29 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the PRC provides: "If a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests appropriate reduction, the people's court shall take the actual losses as the basis, consider comprehensive factors such as the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the expected benefits, and make a ruling in accordance with the principle of fairness and good faith. Where the agreed liquidated damages exceed 30% of the losses caused, they may generally be deemed as 'excessively higher than the losses caused' as provided in Article 114, Paragraph 2 of the Contract Law."

In the original trial, Huilang Company argued that the patent was unilaterally assigned by Liu Junxia and had nothing to do with Huilang Company, and did not request a reduction of the liquidated damages for being excessively high. In the second instance, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Interpretation on Sales Contract Disputes, after this court provided clarification, Huilang Company argued that Langkun Company had not suffered losses due to the breach, and that the liquidated damages stipulated in the contract were excessive, requesting the court to reduce them. Since Langkun Company also failed to submit sufficient evidence to prove the specific circumstances of its actual losses beyond the value of the patent itself, this court holds that the liquidated damages stipulated in the contract are manifestly excessive and should be reduced. Considering Huilang Company's subjective fault in unilaterally assigning the patent, this court determines ex officio that Huilang Company shall pay liquidated damages of RMB 150,000 for its unauthorized assignment of the patent.

In summary, Langkun Company's appeal is well-founded. The facts found in the original trial judgment are basically correct, but the application of law was improper. This court hereby corrects it. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2018) Jing 73 Min Chu No. 1132 of the Beijing Intellectual Property Court;

2. Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay liquidated damages of RMB 150,000 to Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 13,800, to be borne by Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 5,865 and by Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 7,935. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 13,800, to be borne by Beijing Langkun Biotechnology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 5,865 and by Beijing Huilang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 7,935.

This judgment is final.
